style: Mechanical cut-paper illustrations with exact force-distance diagrams
provider: Built-in image generation and deterministic SVG diagrams
note: Images are simplified models, not construction drawings, tool-use instructions or accessibility specifications. Arrows indicate directions unless a caption defines a numerical model. A machine can change force, distance, speed or direction; not every arrangement reduces effort force. Fixed and movable pulley arrangements differ, and supporting rope segments determine the ideal advantage. Ideal examples ignore friction and pulley weight; real input work is greater than useful output work when energy is dissipated. Friction changes mechanical energy into thermal energy rather than destroying it. Object pictures are observation examples. Build only the small, teacher-approved tabletop model described in this edition; do not lift a full water-cooler jug or use sharp tools for the activity.
